transcript:
[00:00] Evan Brooks: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm evan from Redwood AE. jin on the call is our solutions eng.
[00:06] Amira Hassan: hi, i'm amira, head of ai at verdant energy, we run the customer chatbot and outage prediction models.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: liam, platform eng, i own infra and k8s clusters.
[00:16] Priya Menon: priya, security architect.
[00:19] Jin Park: great to meet you all. quick agenda, we'll ask about current stack and pain points, then dig into reliability, failover, and security needs.
[00:28] Amira: sounds good. to start, we currently host an open model on prem in our eu-west-1-ish region, it's sort of self‑managed - k8s, a few gpus, running a trimmed down llama variant. latency has been ok, but we're seeing spikes and we've had two incidents in the last quarter where the KV cash (sic) warmed and we lost state during rollouts.
[00:45] Liam: yes, one incident caused about 7 minutes of elevated error rates while we scrambled a restart. we want a more predictable fallover plan rather than manual scripts.
[00:53] Evan: makes sense. when you say fallover, do you mean to another region, to a lower‑capacity Dedicated pool, or to a hosted variant? all three are common patterns.
[01:03] Amira: ideally multi-region; if eu-west goes down we want traffic to fail to us-west with minimal impact. but we'd also accept a degrading fallback that keeps service up at higher latency if cost is lower.
[01:14] Priya: data residency is a concern for some of our customers; any cross-region failover needs to respect residency constraints and KMS ownership. we cannot replicate sensitive data outside EU for certain tenant segments.
[01:25] Jin: understood. Redwood supports routing policies that can prefer same-region, then fall back to designated regions, and we can also tag models/data paths for residency to prevent cross-border replicas for protected tenants. we also have a private deployment option where the control plane is customer-managed and keys stay in your KMS.
[01:40] Liam: can you clarify the difference between Redwood Dedicated and Private in terms of failover? i've read the docs but the exact behavior under an incident is fuzzy.
[01:48] Evan: sure. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our hosted environment — you get predictable throughput and a capacity pool we reserve for you. if a region loses capacity, routing can fail over to another region or to a lower‑tier capacity pool and we have automated fallback policies. Private means the control plane and runtime are deployed into your VPC or on-prem; you manage the networking but we provide the orchestration. for Private you control which regions replicas exist in and how failover is gated by your network policies.
[02:15] Amira: and SLA? what's the SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:19] Jin: Dedicated has an SLA with uptime and latency SLOs tied to reserved capacity contracts — typical uptime for Dedicated customers is 99.9% with credits for breaches, we can talk specifics in the contract. Hosted (multi-tenant) is lower-tier SLA or best-effort for free tiers. Private SLAs are negotiated because you're running in your infra but we can provide runbooks and support SLAs as part of an enterprise agreement.
[02:40] Priya: what's the expected RTO / RPO for your multi-region failover? we need to model worst-case for executive reporting.
[02:46] Jin: typical automated failover to a pre-warmed region is sub-60s to start routing, but full restoration of KV cache and state can take minutes depending on model and cache size — we use prefix caching and partial response modes to keep latency bounded. for P95 latency we aim to keep it within the contracted SLOs with progressive degradation rather than hard failure.
[03:06] Liam: do you support gradual traffic shifting (canary) during region failover to avoid thundering herd?
[03:11] Evan: yes, we have canary and rate-limited rollouts, and also circuit-breakers that will route a fraction of traffic to fallback to validate performance before a full cutover.
[03:20] Amira: interesting. cost is a big one — we don't want to double spend on always-on cross region replicas. how does Redwood approach cold standby vs warm standby?
[03:30] Jin: you can configure degrees of pre-warming. warm standby keeps a small fleet preloaded with KV cache warmers and preallocated GPU memory so failover is fast but costs more. cold standby spins up on demand and will have slower RTO. we can model the economics: for example warm standby to us‑west would increase monthly cost by roughly X% depending on qps and model size; we'll run numbers for your traffic profile.
[03:50] Priya: about encryption — do you have support for customer-managed keys and HSM? we require AES in transit and at rest plus BYOK for certain workloads.
[03:58] Jin: yes, KMS integrations are supported. Hosted keeps keys in our KMS unless you configure customer-managed keys; Dedicated supports BYOK and Private can be set up with HSM/KMS inside your VPC so keys never leave your boundary. we'll share the SOC 2 and ISO docs and an architecture diagram.
[04:14] Liam: failure modes — what happens if a model variant isn't compatible across regions? e.g., different quantization or kernel support.
[04:21] Jin: good question. Redwood uses model variants with compatibility metadata; routing policies will prefer compatible variants. if exact variant isn't available we'll fall back to a verified compatible model with degraded throughput/latency. that's why model catalog curation is important; we also support on-the-fly compilation and kernel selection but there may be a short warm-up period.
[04:41] Amira: do you expose tracing hooks so we can tie Redwood's traces into our observability stack? we want end-to-end traces for incidents.
[04:48] Evan: yes, we integrate with OpenTelemetry, and you can forward traces/logs into your existing telemetry. the console gives per-route latency and token-level cost breakouts for debugging.
[04:58] Priya: on auditability, we need detailed access logs and immutable audit trails for model version changes.
[05:03] Jin: audit logs with S3 archiving and immutability options are available, and we can configure RBAC and SSO/SAML. we'll capture model rollouts, who triggered them, and tie to CI/CD IDs.
[05:15] Liam: if we did a Private deployment on our VPC, how much effort is expected to maintain orchestration? our team size is small.
[05:22] Evan: Private does require more ops commitment; we offer an optional managed support layer where Redwood handles orchestration and upgrades inside your VPC under an enterprise contract. otherwise you'll be responsible for applying updates and operational runbooks.
[05:36] Amira: timeline — our exec wants a pilot in Q3 to validate incident tolerance. we need to show we can hit P95 < 350ms and failover under 2 minutes for non‑sensitive tenants.
[05:47] Jin: that's doable. Pilot approach: start with Hosted Dedicated reserved pool in eu-west with warm standby in us-west for the pilot, run a chaos test to trigger failover, measure RTO and latency, and then evaluate Private if residency issues arise.
[06:01] Evan: to be concrete, we'll send a proposal with three options: Hosted Dedicated pilot, Dedicated + warm standby, and Private starter kit with managed ops. pricing and SLOs will be included.
[06:11] Amira: great. any gotchas you want us to know?
[06:15] Jin: sometimes folks underestimate KV cache warming time for large models; another is that cross-region networking can add egress and privacy concerns — we can help design a policy that only routes less-sensitive tenants cross-region.
[06:27] Priya: can we get a short writeup of the fallback policy templates you support? we want to map them to our incident runbooks.
[06:33] Evan: yes, we'll include fallback templates and recommended runbook snippets.
[06:37] Amira: ok sounds like a plan. thanks, everyone.
[06:40] Evan: quick recap and next steps: we'll send hosting comparison and pricing, SOC 2/ISO docs, failover diagram and schedule the deep dive. action items we'll capture and follow up. thanks for the time.
[06:52] Jin: last note — i'll run an initial cost estimate based on rough qps, but we'll need your actual traffic numbers.
[06:58] Liam: i'll share a traffic export and P95 numbers after this.
[07:03] Priya: i'll compile the compliance questions and share.
[07:08] Evan: perfect. we'll follow up.
[07:10] [call ends]
